gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-yuji-boku: Red Hat Display draws a marker-like line with visible daylight inside every curve, while Yuji Boku is a serif with cable-thick strokes. Both keep their curves open and their lines uniform.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-yuji-syuku: Red Hat Display holds its marker-like width through every single turn. Yuji Syuku, a serif with open spacing and thin, respectable strokes, sits beneath it and lets the heavier headline do the shouting.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-ibm-plex-serif: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display keeps its line uniform. IBM Plex Serif comes next with slimmer horizontals and a loosened c, so paragraphs move along with a steady, corporate confidence.
gen-fs-sentient-fs-bespoke-sans: Crisp and literary: Sentient has a faint crayon-like rhythm and tightly closed rounds, while Bespoke Sans opens its curves wide. One holds light in; the other lets it pass through.
gen-fs-sharpie-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One brings curvy, open letters beneath Sharpie, whose gap is a hairline crack in porcelain. BhuTuka Expanded One slows the eye to a leisurely walk, its thin joins matching the stems.
gen-fs-sharpie-gf-hepta-slab: Hepta Slab reads wide and quietly unhurried, its open counters breathing into the white space around each stretched-out word. Sharpie's pressed-slot tightness against that openness is the whole story.
gen-fs-sharpie-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: A hairline crack of a gap runs between Sharpie's letters, while Stint Ultra Expanded floats each character apart in open serif forms. Pressed tight up top, then scattered loose below.
gen-fs-stardom-gf-graduate: Dramatic from the first glance, Stardom sets outsized lowercase and hairline counter-strokes against Graduate, whose curves carry no contrast with its stems. Loud hairlines meet uniform strokes; that clash is the point.
gen-fs-styro-gf-epunda-slab: Epunda Slab brings tall, rounded lowercase and gaping curves beneath Styro, whose crowded letters nearly touch each other. Over a full page, the body would feel dignified and gently unhurried.
gen-fs-styro-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla reads refined, its lowercase closely matching the capitals. Against Styro's crowded letters, that lowercase e, opened like a pried clasp, is where the pair finds its strength.
